strengths: Significant scale and vocabulary diversity: Affogato substantially scales up 3D and 2D affordance grounding with 150K 3D assets and over 750K open-vocabulary query-heatmap pairs, overcoming the narrow category constraints (23 classes) of prior benchmarks like 3D AffordanceNet and LASO.

Well-engineered automated generation pipeline (Affogato-Engine): The multi-stage process—leveraging Gemma3 for diverse interaction prompts, Molmo for precise 2D keypoint pointing, SAM for mask generation, and robust multi-view voting to lift 2D predictions into 3D heatmaps—is technically sound and scalable.

Rigorous evaluation and quality control: A subset of 5K query-heatmap pairs was evaluated by human experts, and problematic annotations were manually corrected to establish a reliable, high-quality benchmark test split.

Strong empirical generalization: Models trained on Affogato (Espresso-3D and Espresso-2D) demonstrate superior cross-dataset transferability to LASO and AGD20K, as well as remarkable cross-category generalization on unseen object types (e.g., Daily-Used to Furnitures, and zero-shot transfers).
Thorough supplementary evaluation: The inclusion of Affogato-Partial, background augmentation analysis, and detailed qualitative comparisons effectively contextualizes real-world applicability.
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: The proposed baseline models (Espresso-2D/3D) rely largely on off-the-shelf frozen encoders (PartField, DINOv2, CLIP) combined with standard transformer decoders, serving primarily as baseline demonstrators rather than algorithmic innovations.

Impact of annotation noise on training: The human evaluation indicates approximately 15.4% of raw automated annotations are rated 'not good'. While the test split was manually filtered and refined, the paper lacks an ablation study evaluating the effect of this label noise on training convergence and model robustness.

Discrepancies in cross-dataset metrics: In Table 2, while aIoU and SIM improve or remain relatively consistent under cross-dataset transfer, MAE degrades substantially (e.g., +48.3%p for PointRefer). While the authors reasonably hypothesize that differences in annotation scale cause this, further metric normalization or deeper analysis would make the cross-dataset conclusions more definitive.

strengths: Significantly advances dataset scale and diversity: Prior 3D affordance benchmarks (e.g., 3D AffordanceNet, LASO, OpenAD) have been predominantly constrained to the same ~23 PartNet categories and limited predefined taxonomies. Affogato drastically scales this up to 150K 3D assets and over 750K open-vocabulary query-heatmap pairs across >450 object classes.

Well-engineered automated generation pipeline: The Affogato-Engine smartly leverages complementary foundation models—Gemma 3 for context-aware interaction queries via chain-of-thought, Molmo for precise 2D point grounding, and SAM for mask generation, unified through a multi-view 3D projection and voting aggregation scheme.

Rigorous benchmark quality control: The authors conduct a formal quality assessment with domain experts on 1K objects (5K pairs) and curate a human-inspected and refined test split, ensuring reliable and trustworthy evaluation.

Extensive cross-modality and cross-domain validation: The paper validates the utility of Affogato across both 3D (LASO cross-dataset evaluation, unseen category generalization, and partial view analysis) and 2D benchmarks (AGD20K zero-shot and full fine-tuning), demonstrating superior generalization and transferability compared to existing datasets and methods.
Clear presentation and thorough documentation: The paper and supplementary material provide detailed breakdowns of statistics, failure modes, implementation specifics, and qualitative examples.
weaknesses: Noise in training data from automated generation: The human evaluation study shows that ~15.4% of generated pairs are rated as 'not good' and 12.3% as 'ok'. While the test split is manually verified and refined, the remaining ~149K training objects inherently contain non-negligible label noise, query hallucinations, and segmentation artifacts from the underlying foundation models.

Limited architectural novelty: The proposed Espresso-3D and Espresso-2D models are minimalistic adaptations of existing architectures (e.g., PartField, OOAL, and standard transformer cross-attention decoders with frozen backbones). While serving adequately as baselines, the algorithmic contribution of the modeling aspect itself is modest.

Domain gap to real-world embodied scenarios: The 3D assets are sourced from Objaverse as isolated objects without environmental context, physical interaction dynamics, or realistic scenes. Although background augmentation is applied for 2D images, grounding affordances in complex, cluttered scenes remains an open challenge not fully addressed here.

Representation restricted to contact heatmaps: Affordance is formulated solely as spatial contact/region heatmaps, lacking deeper interaction parameters such as approach direction, post-contact trajectory, articulation degrees of freedom, or contact poses.

strengths: Substantial scale and diversity leap: Prior 3D affordance benchmarks (e.g., 3D AffordanceNet, LASO, OpenAD) have been predominantly constrained to 23 object categories derived from PartNet with closed-vocabulary annotations. Affogato significantly scales this up by leveraging 150K 3D objects from Objaverse, spanning over 450 semantic classes and 350 affordance types with 750K open-vocabulary natural language queries.

Well-designed automated generation pipeline: The Affogato-Engine effectively chains state-of-the-art vision-language models (Gemma3 for CoT query generation, Molmo for precise 2D coordinate pointing, and SAM for mask extraction) coupled with multi-view 3D projection and voting. This multi-view aggregation mitigates single-view occlusion and pointing inconsistency.

Quality control and human-verified benchmark split: The authors perform human evaluation across 1K objects (5K pairs) and specifically curate a high-quality test split where problematic annotations were manually corrected, ensuring that evaluation is grounded against reliable human ground truth rather than unchecked synthetic pseudo-labels.

Strong cross-domain and cross-dataset transfer: Extensive experiments demonstrate clear empirical utility. Models trained on Affogato show superior cross-dataset generalization to LASO compared to the reverse (Table 2), and pre-training on Affogato yields noticeable improvements in 2D affordance grounding on AGD20K across both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings (Table 4).

Thorough auxiliary analyses: The submission includes valuable extensions such as Affogato-Partial to address single-view occlusion scenarios, background augmentation studies (Table A1), and an honest discussion of pipeline failure modes.
weaknesses: Noise inherent to automated pseudo-labeling: Although the test split undergoes manual verification, the training set relies entirely on model-generated annotations. Human evaluation revealed that ~15.4% of generated annotations were rated as 'not good' due to issues like hallucinated functionalities, semantic drift in Gemma3, or SAM edge-bias. The downstream impact of training on this level of label noise is not systematically quantified via noise-filtering ablations.

Limited architectural novelty: The proposed Espresso models are standard configurations of existing vision backbones (PartField, DINOv2) and frozen CLIP text encoders with a conventional transformer cross-attention decoder. While adequate as baselines, the algorithmic contribution of the modeling side is modest.

Cross-dataset evaluation anomalies: In Table 2, while relative drops are smaller for Affogato-trained models, absolute performance when transferring from Affogato to LASO remains low (e.g., Espresso-3D achieves only 0.067 aIoU on LASO vs. 0.136 in-domain). Additionally, MAE increases counterintuitively across transfers; while attributed to scale discrepancies, metric normalization or standardization across datasets would provide a clearer picture.

Absence of real-world 3D scene / robotic validation: Affogato focuses entirely on isolated 3D meshes without contextual backgrounds or physical interaction dynamics (e.g., approach trajectory, gripper pose, applied force), limiting immediate applicability to complex real-world embodied manipulation environments.

strengths: Significance and scale: Affordance grounding in 3D has long been restricted to very small closed-set benchmarks (e.g., 23 classes from PartNet). Affogato-750K scales this up dramatically to 150K 3D assets and 750K query-heatmap pairs covering over 450 object classes and 350 affordance types.

Well-engineered annotation pipeline: Chaining Gemma3 (for CoT-based affordance query formulation), Molmo (for point localization), and MobileSAM (with a smallest-mask selection heuristic) followed by multi-view 3D consensus aggregation is sound, effective, and fully automated.

Rigorous data validation: The authors conduct a careful human verification on a 5K subset (reporting an 84.8% success rate) and provide a detailed categorization and quantitative breakdown of failure modes (e.g., Molmo pointing errors, Gemma3 misidentifications, SAM edge bias).

Consistent transfer gains: Pretraining on Affogato-750K yields clear improvements for both Espresso models and existing baselines (OpenAD, PointRefer, AffordanceNet), with especially notable gains on unseen categories in both 3D (LASO) and 2D (AGD20K).

Thorough analysis: The paper includes essential sanity checks, such as filtering out evaluation-category overlap (Table 5), ablaing the effect of pretraining data scale (Table A3), point resolution (Table A2), and testing zero-shot transfer to real-world cluttered robot scenes (Open X-Embodiment).
weaknesses: Inconsistent naming artifacts: In multiple figures (Figure 1 diagram, Figure 6 column header, and Figure A4), the model is referred to as 'Gato-3D' and 'Gato-2D' rather than 'Espresso-3D' / 'Espresso-2D', indicating an incomplete renaming pass before submission.

Synthetic-to-real and isolated-object limitation: Because the dataset relies on isolated 3D object meshes from Objaverse rendered on clean/random backgrounds, it does not naturally model scene context, multi-object relationships, or environmental constraints.

Mixed results on seen benchmarks: While unseen generalization improves across the board, pretraining on Affogato-750K leads to minor degradations on some seen metrics (e.g., PointRefer on LASO seen drops by 0.6 aIoU and 2.9 SIM; Espresso-3D AUC drops slightly by 0.1, and MAE increases).

strengths: Substantial scale and diversity leap: Affogato-750K scales open-vocabulary affordance grounding to 150K 3D objects and 750K annotations across more than 450 object classes, breaking the long-standing limitation of existing 3D benchmarks that were constrained to 23 PartNet categories.

Well-designed and scalable automated annotation pipeline: Chaining a vision-language model (Gemma 3) with chain-of-thought prompt design, a spatial pointing model (Molmo), part-level segmentation (MobileSAM), and multi-view consensus aggregation effectively suppresses single-view errors and yields high-quality 3D heatmaps.

Rigorous data quality and benchmark construction: The authors include a human-verified 5K test set, a transparent failure mode analysis (84.8% human-agreement success rate), and a thorough held-out category filtering experiment (Table 5) confirming that gains stem from representation learning at scale rather than label leakage.

Consistent cross-modal and cross-architecture transfer: Pretraining on Affogato-750K provides solid and consistent gains across both 2D (AGD20K) and 3D (LASO) benchmarks, improving not only the proposed Espresso models but also existing methods such as OpenAD, PointRefer, and AffordanceNet.
weaknesses: Architectural novelty of Espresso is limited: Espresso-2D and Espresso-3D are straightforward combinations of pretrained encoders (DINOv2, PartField, CLIP) with standard cross-attention decoders. While intentionally minimal to isolate dataset contributions, the algorithmic contribution of the modeling side is modest.

Inconsistency in training description: In Section 4 (page 9), the text states regarding Espresso-3D that 'we finetune both the pretrained 3D vision encoder and text encoder during training', whereas Appendix B.2 (page 21) states 'We used the official pretrained checkpoint and froze the entire vision backbone during training'. This discrepancy should be clarified.

Synthetic object-centric domain gap: The dataset is built on isolated Objaverse meshes lacking physical context, occlusion, and interaction dynamics (forces, pre-grasp poses, or articulated mechanisms). While background augmentation and zero-shot robot workspace tests (Figure 7) partially mitigate this, the lack of full scene context remains an inherent constraint for real-world robotics.

Minor cosmetic and naming inconsistencies: In multiple figures (e.g., Figure 1, Figure 6, Figure A4), the model is referred to as 'Gato-3D' and 'Gato-2D' rather than 'Espresso-3D' and 'Espresso-2D', indicating an incomplete renaming pass.

strengths: Significance of dataset scale and diversity: Affogato-750K substantially scales up affordance grounding data (>450 object classes, >350 affordances, 150K 3D assets, 750K annotations), breaking the bottleneck of prior 3D benchmarks that were constrained to ~23 PartNet object classes and closed-vocabulary annotations.

Well-engineered annotation pipeline: The multi-stage pipeline sensibly combines recent foundation models (Gemma-3 for contextual query generation, Molmo for 2D interaction pointing, MobileSAM for mask extraction) with multi-view 3D consensus aggregation, which effectively filters out single-view pointing inaccuracies.

Rigorous evaluation and ablation studies: The paper provides thorough empirical validation across both 3D (LASO) and 2D (AGD20K) benchmarks, including out-of-domain evaluation on human-verified test data, scaling-law experiments (Table A3), and a leak-filtering experiment (Table 5) verifying that pretraining benefits are not simply due to label overlap.

Comprehensive quality control and error analysis: A 5K human-verified test split is curated, accompanied by a detailed quantification of pipeline failure modes (e.g., 34.9% from 2D pointing inaccuracies, 36.8% from query/misidentification errors in Stage 1).
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: The Espresso baseline models (Espresso-3D and Espresso-2D) largely assemble existing off-the-shelf vision/text backbones (PartField, DINOv2, CLIP, Recap-CLIP) with standard cross-attention decoders. While the authors state this is intentional to isolate dataset impact, the methodological contribution on the modeling side remains modest.

Synthetic-to-real domain gap: The dataset is derived exclusively from isolated synthetic Objaverse 3D models with rendered views. Although background augmentation is applied for 2D transfer and qualitative results on Open X-Embodiment are shown, the pipeline does not address complex real-world scenes containing multi-object occlusions, cluttered environments, or incomplete sensor scans.

Potential bias from the smallest-mask selection heuristic: Stage 3 defaults to selecting SAM's smallest mask hypothesis to target precise contact points. While this works well for handles and buttons, it can cause systematic under-segmentation for large contact areas (e.g., 'sit on', 'lie on', or supporting surfaces).

Minor inconsistencies in presentation: There are noticeable naming discrepancies in the figures where the models are referred to as 'Gato-3D' / 'Gato-2D' (e.g., in Figure 1, Figure 6, and Figure A4) and 'Affo-150K' (in Figure 1), reflecting incomplete cleanup during manuscript revision.
